paragraphs.text: A **cash-secured put** is a short put in which the writer sets aside enough cash to buy the shares at the strike price if the put is assigned [S1]. The writer sells the put, collects the premium up front, and accepts the obligation to buy 100 shares per contract at the strike any time before expiration [S1]. A **naked put**, or short put on margin, is the same contract, but the broker holds only a margin requirement, a fraction of the purchase price, instead of the full purchase price [S4]. **Assignment** is the process by which an option writer is selected to fulfil the obligation of a contract that a holder has exercised [S2]. A **poor man's covered call** is a two-leg position: a long, deep in-the-money LEAPS call and a short, near-term, out-of-the-money call on the same stock [S3].

This run allocated the strategy budget across cash-secured puts and LEAPS legs, with cash left in reserve. The regime label is normal, with a risk-free rate of {{regime.risk_free_rate_pct|pct}} and a VIX of {{regime.vix}} at the {{regime.vix_percentile}}th percentile. The account value is {{profile.account_value|money}} and the account type is {{profile.account_type}}.

The good-to-own quality gate is a filter, not a discovery engine: it decides which tickers are allowed into the option screeners at all, records a reason for every rejection, and produces a score for the survivors [S5]. The product promise is "stocks you would be happy to own if assigned" [S5].

{{quality_screen.passed_count}} underlyings passed the quality screen: {{quality_screen.passed_tickers|list}}. {{quality_screen.excluded_count}} were excluded, with the reasons given as {{quality_screen.excluded|list}}. The trend board is a secondary signal only; the trending tickers in the errors list, such as {{errors[0]}}, were skipped because they are not on the good-to-own list.

The app watches public conversation on Reddit, X, Wikipedia pageviews, Google Trends and news feeds for rising discussion of products and brands, resolves that discussion to tickers, and produces a consumer-trend score [S6]. For the structure of a short put, a surging consumer-trend score is closer to the opposite of a good candidate, and the app is built around that fact [S6].

The bottleneck board is a secondary signal: it re-orders quality-gated stocks, never adds one. The top-scoring layer is {{bottlenecks.layers[0].name}} at {{bottlenecks.layers[0].score}}, with thesis state {{bottlenecks.layers[0].thesis_state}}. The networking layer, {{bottlenecks.layers[5].name}}, scores {{bottlenecks.layers[5].score}} with thesis state {{bottlenecks.layers[5].thesis_state}}, and its company {{bottlenecks.companies[4].ticker}} carries flags {{bottlenecks.companies[4].flags|list}}. {{counts.positions_sized}} positions were sized, so no bottleneck flag applies to a sized position in this run.

No position was sized: the sizer reports {{risk.sizing_flags|list}}, and the warning states {{risk.warnings[0]}}. The skipped candidates include {{skipped_candidates[0].candidate_id}}, with a realistic loss of one contract of {{skipped_candidates[0].realistic_loss_per_contract|money}}, and {{skipped_candidates[2].candidate_id}}, with a realistic loss of one contract of {{skipped_candidates[2].realistic_loss_per_contract|money}}. {{counts.skipped_total}} candidates were skipped in total.

The risk picture shows {{risk.checks_passed}} of {{risk.checks_total}} checks passed, with a short-put notional of {{risk.checks[0].value|percent}} against a limit of {{risk.checks[0].limit|percent}} and margin usage of {{risk.checks[1].value|percent}} against a limit of {{risk.checks[1].limit|percent}}. A {{risk.stress[-10%].shock}} move with a {{risk.stress[-10%].iv_shock}} IV shock gives {{risk.stress[-10%].pnl|money}}, a {{risk.stress[-20%].shock}} move gives {{risk.stress[-20%].pnl|money}}, and a {{risk.stress[-30%].shock}} move gives {{risk.stress[-30%].pnl|money}}, with a realistic loss drop threshold of {{risk.realistic_loss_drop_pct|pct}}.
